comments.content: The conditional operator is misused here: each branch is a parenthesized comma expression, so everything before the last operand is evaluated and discarded. The ternary therefore resolves to `sdslen(...) - c->qb_pos` (size_t) in the hidden case and to a `char *` pointer into the query buffer in the normal case. Besides the compile-time "pointer/integer type mismatch in conditional expression" diagnostic, the two strings are never used as the format string, and the real format arguments are lost (e.g. `%zu`/`%.*s` have no matching arguments), which is undefined behavior and can crash/garbage-print. Also note `%.*s` with `PROTO_DUMP_LEN` (128) halves is unrelated to the 256-byte `buf`, but that is pre-existing. Use an explicit if/else instead of a ternary over snprintf calls.
comments.existing_code:
snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), server.hide_user_data_from_log ?
                     ("Query buffer during protocol error: [hide_user_data_from_log]Redacted %zu bytes",
                      sdslen(c->querybuf) - c->qb_pos) :
                     ("Query buffer during protocol error: '%.*s' (... more %zu bytes ...) '%.*s'",
                      PROTO_DUMP_LEN / 2, c->querybuf + c->qb_pos, sdslen(c->querybuf) - c->qb_pos - PROTO_DUMP_LEN,
                      PROTO_DUMP_LEN / 2, c->querybuf + sdslen(c->querybuf) - PROTO_DUMP_LEN / 2));
